title: In search of lost time, Proust
subject: litterature
description: Seven volumes, 1.5 million words: Proust explores involuntary memory and makes time the main character of the novel.

hero.hook: A madeleine dipped in tea. And suddenly, a whole childhood comes back.

blocks.text: **In search of lost time**, from **1913** to **1927**, counts **7 volumes**, **3 200 pages** and **1.5 million words**. **Marcel Proust** moves the novel towards interiority, the inner world of thoughts and sensations. He places the **[[Involuntary memory]]**, a memory triggered by a sensation such as a taste or a smell, at the center of the story.

Time is no longer a simple setting: it becomes the main character of a metaphysical adventure, a reflection on the nature of time and memory. Proust shows how the past survives in us, hidden in sensations. Reading Research means accepting a slow pace, made up of tiny details that suddenly open up entire worlds.

**Marcel Proust** attends the **[[Salons]]**, meetings of Parisian high society around art and politics, then isolates himself after the death of his mother in **1905**. He lines his room with cork to protect himself from noise and pollen, and writes there at night.

blocks.caption: Marcel Proust: recluse writer in the service of memory.

blocks.text: Proust died while correcting his proofs, asking his servant Céleste to add “paperoles” to the margins to lengthen his texts.

The first volume, **From Swann**, published in **1913**, was rejected by publishers. , writer and figure of the **NRF**, a literary magazine, would later admit to having made a serious error in disdaining the manuscript. **[[André Gide]]**

sections.title: The madeleine and the living memory

blocks.text: Proust distinguishes voluntary memory, a “cold” memory reconstituted by effort, from , provoked by a sensation. The **madeleine** soaked in tea resurrects **Combray**, childhood village, in its emotional entirety. **[[Involuntary memory]]**

blocks.caption: The madeleine: the most famous trigger of involuntary memory.

blocks.text: And suddenly the memory came to me.
blocks.attribution: Marcel Proust, On the Swann Side

blocks.text: The past is not dead: it is deposited in us in objects or sensations. The writer must translate these impressions into language. Proust was obsessed with smells and sometimes perfumed his mail to preserve his letters from time. This sensory attention transforms the novel into an exploration of consciousness.

The Research analyzes the decay, the decline, of the aristocracy and snobbery. The narrator, often called **Marcel**, navigates between the side of **Swann**, the bourgeoisie, and that of the **Guermantes**, the great nobility.

Love is a disease of the imagination, inseparable from jealousy. , complex aristocrat, introduces previously taboo themes. Proust describes a society of secrets and masks, where everyone plays a role dictated by their desires and their social rank. Long social evenings become laboratories of human vanity. **[[Monsieur de Charlus]]**

The seventh volume, , provides the final answer. New involuntary memories reveal to the narrator his vocation: to write the work we have just read. Art alone can rescue lived moments from the destruction of time. **[[time rediscovered by art]]**

blocks.text: In Proust, lost time is not just the past. It is also time badly spent, dispersed in habits. Art, by fixing a true sensation in a text, finally makes it readable and lasting. The Search influences the novel of the entire 20th century: **Virginia Woolf**, **Jorge Luis Borges** and many others take up the idea of ​​a deep memory, buried in the body.
**In search of lost time**: **1.5 million words** to show that only art, through , can save the past from destruction by time. **[[Involuntary memory]]**
